items.description: US natural gas: marketed production, NGPL production (gaseous equivalent) and dry production; NGPL extraction as share of marketed gas was 0.0912 in 2025 (derived NGPL/marketed; 2023 and 2024 about 0.0825 and 0.0884)
items.note: EIA table rows 'Marketed Production', 'NGPL Production, Gaseous Equivalent', 'Dry Production': 2025: 43,229,110 / 3,941,527 / 39,287,583 (dry = marketed minus NGPL). Shrinkage fraction derived by division.

items.description: US natural gas plant fuel as a share of marketed production, 2024 (arithmetic on EIA volumes; denominator is all marketed gas, not only gas processed)
items.note: Derived by me. Table 1 (2024): 'Plant fuel 484,359' MMcf; 'Marketed production 41,383,893'; 'Total gross withdrawals 45,867,761'. 484,359 / 41,383,893 = 1.17%; versus gross withdrawals 1.06%. Table 14: '2024 Total ... Plant fuel 484,359'; the 2020-2023 plant fuel (518,913; 480,658; 467,511; 474,788 MMcf) is of the same order. Gas actually processed is not reported in these tables, so the share of processed gas would differ.

items.description: US natural gas plant liquids extraction shrinkage (NGPL gaseous equivalent) as a share of marketed production, 2024; combined with plant fuel about 10 %
items.note: Derived by me. Table 1 (2024): 'NGPL production, gaseous equivalent 3,658,962' MMcf; 'Marketed production 41,383,893'; note: 'Total dry production volumes are equal to marketed production minus NGPL production.' 3,658,962 / 41,383,893 = 8.84%; plus plant fuel 1.17% = 10.0% total plant fuel and shrinkage against marketed gas. Includes liquids from rich gas and gas not run through plants in the denominator; no GPSA or per-plant percentage found.
